$comment: Review REQUEST contract v1 (2026-10-06, wiki spec--review-revamp R5; build record R5-FINAL). The reviewer's unit of work is the REQUEST a Dispatch creates (projects/{p}/requests/{trace_id}); the OP chain (projects/{p}/operations/{op_id}, append-only per op) carries the model state; ONE service (apps/pdfmarkuptool/functions/src/review/requests.ts + requestStore.ts) moves both, and nothing else writes either. Ink is the project's markups (projects/{p}/documents/{d}/markups/{id}) plus `request_id`; owned ink (request_id set, its request not `editing`) takes no client write. Every rule the engine applies is a row below: lookup by verb (+ case) -> the rows whose `from` holds the status of `record` (`request` or `op`; `creates` rows need no request) -> without a case, a caseless row wins over cased ones, else case-required -> the first row listing the actor. Invariant keys: inkLock set|clear (ink request_id written in the same transaction; set refuses `owned`), lease take|renew|clear|drop (take mints a new token; renew and clear CAS on the caller's token -> `lease-lost`; drop removes a lease without a token: a reviewer's Release), takeover (a take from a leased status needs the lease expired or held by the same worker), cas (call fields that must equal the record's current value), createsOp (a new op in the same transaction; `of` from the latestOp entry that matched), latestOp (the request's latest op must match one entry), latestOpNot (its status must not be one of these), notReleased, setsReleased, attemptsBelow / attemptsInc / renderAttemptsInc (limits), alsoRequest (D8: the same verdict moves the request too), keepsStatus, noHistory, noCalls (beats keep no idempotency entry), message (the thread entry type). The reviewer's REPLY (2026-10-07) is `request.post [correction]`: from proposed, needs-you, or a failed apply it sends the request back to the drafter (queued -> proposal n+1). RELEASE is the one way to give ink back: before Accept and after a failed apply (`failed-apply`: nothing was applied) it cancels the request and frees the ink; once a change landed (`accepted`) it hides the ink with the request; after a Restore took the change back out (`restored`, 2026-10-09: a restore applied or rendered, or a failed reapply on top of one -- the model no longer holds the change) it cancels the request and frees the ink like `failed-apply`, so the reviewer's ink comes back free to edit and Send again. `request.reopen` stays in the table (records already `editing` still Send again) but no client offers it. Vendored byte-identical to apps/pdfmarkuptool/functions/src/review/ (requestContract.test.ts), pdf-cli internal/reviewcore/ and the drafter's scripts/worker/ (R5-1 part 2 / R5-2). R6 (2026-10-07, additive, requestVersion unchanged; wiki spec--review-revamp R6): the same records on Firestore -- number.counterDoc (the counter off the project doc), limits.docBytes (refusal too-large), refusal contention (a store transaction that kept aborting; retry with the same op_id), reads worker.poll, and clientWrites (what a client may not write on a gated project, for firestore.rules, the local guard and the SPA alike). 2026-10-08 (additive): `progress` + limits.progress -- the live-steps line, until then hand-typed in the engine, the drafter and pdf-cli. 2026-10-09 (requestVersion unchanged, like the 2026-10-07 Release split; only a reviewer calls request.release): the `restored` Release case, split out of `accepted` -- Release after a successful Restore gave the ink back hidden, throwing the reviewer's intent away (prod tr-mec3fpo4kplia4lhaklf).

number.$comment: U2 (2026-10-07): the request's per-project NUMBER, the `#4` a reviewer reads on the canvas badge, the rail row and the toasts. The creating move assigns it in its own transaction: 1 + the project doc's `counter` (the highest number assigned so far; absent = 0), and writes the counter back in that transaction, so two concurrent Dispatches get distinct numbers (the second one's transaction retries). Never reused, never changed by a later verb; a released or cancelled request keeps its number. Optional on a record: requests created before this field render without a number. The counter is service-only (firestore.rules, local/src/opsRules.ts). R6: the counter lives in its own doc, requests/{counterDoc} (field `counter`), not on the project doc -- every request transaction reads the project doc for the gate, so a counter there tied each Dispatch to every other request transaction; a project-doc `counter` from before R6 is read once as the floor. counterDoc is not a request: readers skip any id without the trace prefix.

clientWrites.$comment: R6: what a CLIENT may not write on a project with the gate -- one list for the three enforcers: firestore.rules (the helpers apps/pdfmarkuptool/scripts/gen-rules-review-request.mjs generates), the local server's guard (local/src/opsRules.ts) and the SPA's gated write path (services/markupFields.ts strips them). inkFields: never written by a client, create or update -- the ink field only the request service writes (inkField) and the v8 review fields the SPA projects onto ink in memory (the R2 dispatch lock + its released flag, trace_id). inkStateFields: the v8 review state the SPA also projects: an update never touches it, a create carries at most the fresh state every create pipeline writes (the v8 default status, an empty history). refusedWhenGated: the v8 client collections a gated project closes (its reviewer actions go through the request service). On EVERY project: inkField, gate.field and number.counter are service-only, and the requests collection is member-read and service-written.

ids.$comment: D2: deterministic ids so a retried call lands on the same record. trace_id = trace.prefix + base32(sha256(projectId + ':' + op_id))[0..length]; a created op = op.prefix + base32(sha256(trace_id + ':' + kind + ':' + n + ':' + seq))[0..length] (n = the accepted proposal, seq = the request's op count before it). base32 = RFC 4648, lowercase alphabet below, no padding. op_id is the CALLER's call id (one per tap / per worker step).

progress.$comment: 2026-10-08 (the live-steps line, #481): `field` is the drafter's one-line progress on a working request ("Step 4 . 0:31 -- Searching the content library"). Only `verb` (request.beat, holder only) writes it: a string of at most limits.progress, kept by a beat that omits it (the lease thread's beats), dropped with `stage` when the request leaves working. Display only (the rail's state line); nothing reads it as state.

proposal.$comment: D6: alternatives[0] is the primary request; each alternative carries its own footprint + cursor (required for the drivers below) and its own inverse (no restore_plan -> no Restore). 2026-10-17 (additive, requestVersion unchanged; wiki spec--drafter-photo-survey 3e): an alternative may carry `items` [{key, label, approx?, warning?}] (at most maxItems, keys unique, label and warning at most limits.summary) -- DISPLAY DATA only, the card's checklist: nothing reads it at Accept and no op carries it; unticking items posts an ordinary request.post [correction] "Leave out: <labels>". 2026-10-19 (additive, requestVersion unchanged; wiki spec--drafter-product-survey "The card, Accept, Restore", A1, slice S8): an item may carry ONE `image` {asset, w, h} -- its evidence picture (photo crop | product page image | our model); `asset` is a promoted photo's reference in the form a markup's media item uses (64 lowercase hex = sha256 of the JPEG at projects/{p}/assets/{asset}.jpg; itemImage.assetRe = asset-contract.json assetRe), w and h integer pixels 1..itemImage.maxEdge (= asset-contract.json limits.edge); other keys are dropped. DISPLAY DATA only, like `items`: nothing reads it at Accept and no op carries it; a malformed image is refused bad-args like a malformed item.

reads.$comment: Read verbs (no transaction writes): any member of the project (owner or an active permission of any role) or the drafter.

worker.poll.$comment: R6: the worker's one read per tick -> {working, queued, ops: {queued, applied}} (requests by status; request-contract ops only).

cardStates.$comment: D9: the card a request shows = its status, and once accepted its latest op (ops sorted by seq). First matching row wins. `stage` overrides the request's stage on the card; `error` = show the op's error.user_text; `renderFailed` applies to a latest op in its `status` whose render_attempts reached limits.renderAttempts. `released` hides the card (history only).

renderFailed.user_text: Applied, but the sheet did not refresh
